title: Soft tissue ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look under the skin: fat, muscles, lymph nodes, and lumps. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: If you feel a lump, have swollen lymph nodes, or have swelling, pain, or puffiness after an injury.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: Exactly where the lump or swelling is and when it appeared
If its size has changed and if it hurts
If you had injuries or surgery in that area
If you had an ultrasound before. Bring the report

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put cream on the area on the day of the scan.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that are easy to take off or lift over the area.

bring: Past ultrasounds and reports, if you have them
A towel or tissues, if you like
steps: You show the doctor the area that bothers you
You lie or sit so the area is easy to check
Gel is put on the skin
The probe is moved over the area and around it
Sometimes it is compared with the same area on the other side
The gel is wiped off with a tissue
feel: Cool gel and light pressure from the probe
If the area is sore, pressing may feel unpleasant. Tell the doctor
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually given right away
If more detail is needed, the doctor may suggest a needle biopsy or another test

faq.q: Is a lump under the skin dangerous?
faq.a: Most often it is harmless, such as a fatty lump or a lymph node. The ultrasound helps the doctor tell what it is.
Usually not. Just come in comfortable clothes.

reminders.text: Soft tissue ultrasound tomorrow. No prep needed. Do not put cream on the area.
